research_rationale: EO 10955 (31 July 1961) has two operative sections: sec. 1 delegates to the Secretary of State the functions conferred on the President by sections 2 and 3 of the Act of September 8, 1960 (Latin America development and reconstruction of Chile), and sec. 2 deems the funds appropriated under those sections allocated to the Secretary of State. The held original (26 FR 6967, jobs/fr-originals text) was read in full for these two sections; the dossier inventory listed only sec. 2 and is corrected to sec. 1 and sec. 2. Later EO 10973 (3 November 1961; 26 FR 10469; official FR text layer) sec. 605(c) lists EO 10955 among orders that "are hereby superseded", and sec. 607 makes that order effective as of September 30, 1961. EO 10973 sec. 101 itself delegates to the Secretary of State the functions under the Latin America act, so the command moved into the new order. Status: no. First end 1961-09-30 by express supersession (effective date from sec. 607, not the signing date of November 3, 1961).
savings_reason: EO 10973 sec. 606 saves determinations, authorizations and other actions made with respect to any function affected by that order and not revoked before its date, to continue until amended, modified or terminated; the delegated functions themselves continue under EO 10973 sec. 101. The surviving effect is therefore carried by EO 10973, not by EO 10955, and no independent EO 10955 command remains.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the number 10955 (cruden-style search recorded in LOOKUPS.md: three held texts, being EO 10955 itself, EO 10973 in two copies) and the dossier's later-event chain; no earlier revocation, amendment, expiry or completion appears. The order has no own-terms end. The only ending instrument is EO 10973 sec. 605(c), effective as of September 30, 1961 under sec. 607, so the first end for both sections is 1961-09-30, not the later signing date (November 3, 1961) or publication date.
scope_check: Both sections are superseded in whole: sec. 605(c) names Executive Order No. 10955 of July 31, 1961 without exception (unlike sec. 605(a), which excepts Part II of EO 10893). No part of EO 10955 is left outside the supersession. The bounded searches current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr returned no citation of EO 10955 and later-events:ofr_catalog returned one superseded-by note, consistent with this.
independent_command_check: Sec. 1 (delegation of functions) and sec. 2 (allocation of funds) are independent commands, each re-checked: sec. 1 is covered by EO 10973 sec. 101 which re-delegates the Latin America act functions to the Secretary of State, and sec. 2 had no separate sunset or independent term. Both are within the one supersession; there is no surviving command in EO 10955.

research_rationale: EO 12082 (19 September 1978; 43 FR 42727) suspends five Title 10 provisions (sec. 1-101) and makes three disability-separation conditions effective (sec. 1-102), each for the period beginning on September 15, 1978 and ending on September 30, 1979, and revokes four earlier orders (sec. 1-103). The held original (fr-originals text of 43 FR 42727) was read in full. Both periodic commands end under the order's own terms at the end of September 30, 1979 (recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading is that they end when that day begins, i.e. 1979-10-01), nothing in the order extends them, and sec. 1-103 was a one-time revocation done on issuance. EO 12239 (21 September 1980; 45 FR 62967) then revoked EO 12082 by name ("No. 12082 is hereby revoked.") and itself suspends the same provisions for October 1, 1979 to September 30, 1982, a separate later command. The revocation is the formal disposition (about a year after the order had run out), not the first end. Status: no; first end 1979-09-30, own terms.
savings_reason: Neither EO 12082 nor EO 12239 contains a saving clause. Promotions and separations carried out during the period are completed acts, not continuing commands, and the four orders revoked by sec. 1-103 stay revoked. Bounded search found no independent surviving command.
earlier_end_check: The own-terms end (September 30, 1979) is earlier than any other event, so it controls. Searched held texts for the number 12082: EO 12082 itself and EO 12239 only (LOOKUPS.md); no earlier revocation, extension of the period or statutory lapse earlier than September 30, 1979 appears. EO 12239 of 1980-09-21 revokes the order after it had expired and is recorded as a later event and the formal disposition, not as the first end. The extension of the suspensions from October 1, 1979 was done by EO 12239 as a new command; it did not extend this order's period.
scope_check: Each periodic clause carries the same period language, so all five suspensions in sec. 1-101 and all three conditions in sec. 1-102 end together at the end of September 30, 1979; no item is excepted or carries a different term. Sec. 1-103 is a one-time revocation with no period. No amendment of EO 12082 appears in the held searches (later-events:ofr_catalog returned only the EO 12239 revocation notes).
independent_command_check: Independent commands checked: sec. 1-101 (suspensions) and sec. 1-102 (conditions made effective) are bounded by the same stated period; sec. 1-103 (revocation of EOs 10616, 11151, 11437 and 11554 as amended) is a completed act on issuance and does not depend on the periods. EO 12239's later revocation of EO 12082 does not revive those four orders, and nothing in EO 12239 says it does.
